key_insight: A small, clinically meaningful set of easy-to-collect features can help large language models screen chronic kidney disease in a zero-shot setting without dataset-specific training.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support practical CKD screening in community and resource-limited settings where full clinical workups and labeled datasets are hard to obtain.
method: Selected a compact subset of relevant variables using machine-learning-based feature analysis
Serialized tabular patient records into standardized text prompts for zero-shot LLM inference
Compared LLaMA-3, Qwen-3, Mistral, and GPT-4o-mini using full vs selected feature sets across three CKD datasets
evidence_signal: Across three heterogeneous datasets from three countries, the selected feature set consistently improved balanced accuracy and probability estimates, with statistically significant gains across models.
watch_item: Results are promising for screening, but real-world deployment still needs careful validation for population shifts, prompt robustness, and clinical workflow integration.
paper_title: From Many to Meaningful: Feature-Guided Zero-Shot Chronic Kidney Disease Screening Using Large Language Models
